channel.title: Mohammed Mudassir Uddin: blog
channel.description: What I built, what broke, what I learned.

item.title: Three certificates, and what each was for
item.description: CS50x, Anthropic's Claude architect exam and two Neo4j certifications. None of them is research. Each covered a specific layer of what I build.

item.title: Where the global layer goes decides when a hybrid learns to retrieve
item.description: Our ICLR 2027 submission: 49 small models, 15 designs, one mechanism changed at a time. Attention-sink size did not predict recall. Layer order and key binding did.

item.title: Four validated upgrades that don't add up
item.description: LAF-YOLOv10 combined four published small-object detection techniques in one detector. Together they cost 7.8 points of mAP, and the loss traces to one interaction.

item.title: LaTeX to Word without losing the equations
item.description: Nine months of work, now on the VS Code Marketplace: editable equations, live cross-references, and failed builds explained in plain words.

item.title: Instructions hidden in log fields
item.description: Guardian-AI v3.0 sits between untrusted security telemetry and the LLM that reads it. A regex list catches the obvious attacks. The rest need layers.

item.title: Flood and fire damage per property, from two Sentinel-2 passes
item.description: AlphaEarth goes from cloud-masked composites to damage tiers for each parcel, and scores itself against independent damage records.

item.title: A data node where the text never leaves the device
item.description: Collecting Telugu, Tamil, Hindi and Bengali text for training without shipping anyone's health records to a server. The rule is one line; enforcing it took four separate guards.

item.title: I audited my own paper
item.description: HAGD's search is fast. The circuit it found in GPT-2 Small kept no more behaviour than random features, and the preprint's larger results were not in the code. What the audit found, and what I changed.

item.title: What our AgentCompress notebook shows, and what it doesn't
item.description: The paper's benchmark is not public, so the released notebook runs on synthetic workflows and its numbers are lower. Both columns belong in the README.

item.title: Four proposals, one question each
item.description: What the proposals we sent to Google, Amazon and GARA this year each set out to answer, including the one that names its own likely negative result.

item.title: Vak joins the Sarvam AI startup program
item.description: An AI literacy and interpretability platform built natively in Telugu and Hindi, not translated from an English tool.

item.title: Done with the degree
item.description: Three years of diploma, three years of engineering, and the two habits they gave me.

item.title: Does the explanation predict the model?
item.description: In May I began working with Prof. Hamdi Al-Jamimi at KFUPM on a narrow question about sepsis decision support: when a model explains itself, is the explanation true?

item.title: Flood claims from radar in under five minutes
item.description: At the 418 Hackathon at Mahindra University we built OrbitClaim Sentinel: Sentinel-1 radar in, a flood-claim decision out, in a JSON small enough to downlink.

item.title: Looking for two people who work below the framework
item.description: We were preparing proposals for the Google TPU Research Awards and the Amazon Research Awards, so I asked for collaborators who care about memory hierarchies and kernels.

item.title: A cost check for code an agent wrote
item.description: At the OpenAI Codex Community Hackathon in Hyderabad we built Gravity, a FinOps check that runs before AI-written code is merged.

item.title: Overdue is not a status
item.description: A small tool for compliance analysts, and the one modelling decision in it that I would defend in any review.

item.title: Four pull requests to pyGAM, starting with the p-values
item.description: Generalized additive models report p-values for their smooth terms. Getting those right needs Wood's rank-r eigendecomposition.

item.title: Eleven pull requests to pgmpy in one week
item.description: Reading a causal-inference library closely enough to fix it, from d-separators to NaN treatment effects.

item.title: Blocking ads on every device from a Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W
item.description: Pi-hole filters ads at the DNS level at home, and Tailscale carries the same filter to my phone when I am out. About two hours of setup.

item.title: An AI chief of staff in 36 hours
item.description: At the Hack-Nation Global AI Hackathon with the MIT Sloan AI Club we mapped how information moves inside a company. The RAG pipeline died at hour 22.

item.title: Searching a hierarchy instead of the graph
item.description: HAGD, our circuit-extraction preprint: cluster the attribution graph, search it from the top, and report a circuit only after it passes causal tests.

item.title: Not every agent step needs the whole model
item.description: AgentCompress picks a precision for each step of an LLM agent's workflow, from the first 32 tokens of the request.

item.title: Pruning for the disease, not for ImageNet
item.description: Our first preprint of the year keeps the channels that separate one leaf disease from another, so a few-shot model fits on a Raspberry Pi 4.

item.title: A PDF in, a training series out
item.description: At the ElevenLabs Worldwide Hackathon in Hyderabad we turned long training documents into short narrated video episodes.

item.title: 2,300 developers, one room, and a fraud-detection agent
item.description: Agentathon 2025 set a Guinness World Record for the largest agentic AI hackathon. What I built there, and the one design idea I kept.
